key_insight: The paper unifies density-ratio estimation and transport-based distribution shift modeling by expressing the log density ratio as the negative Stein operator applied to a displacement field, yielding a single convex estimation problem.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to correct samplers or fit layered transformations under distribution shift without retraining from scratch, which is useful in simulation-based inference and model adaptation.
method: Parametrize the log density ratio via a displacement field acting on the base distribution through the Stein operator.
Solve a convex optimization problem that jointly estimates statistical density shift and dynamical transport.
Iterate estimate-and-move to form two algorithms: push-forward for sampler correction and pull-back for progressively transforming data toward the base.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports applications to distribution shift in simulation-based inference and nonlinear independent component analysis, indicating the approach is evaluated on representative shift and disentanglement tasks.
watch_item: The iterative estimate-and-move scheme may be sensitive to approximation quality, since post-processing and repeated transport steps can accumulate error or require careful initialization.
paper_title: Density Ratio Estimation with Stein Displacement Fields
